quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what should you do?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let other traffic pass before you enter the intersection.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign do?

options.text: Warns of dangers ahead.
Alerts drivers to school zones.
Alerts drivers to parks and recreation areas.
Alerts drivers to gas stations and restaurants.

questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn you about hazards ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Use your horn to alert other drivers.
Watch ahead and stay far behind other cars.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch ahead and stay far behind other cars.
questions.explanation: Staying far behind other cars gives you time to react to problems without sudden stops. This keeps the driver behind you safe too.

questions.question: How much space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signal.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn, but you are not in the correct lane. What should you do?

options.text: Cut across traffic quickly to make your turn.
Turn on your signal and turn from your current lane.
Go to the next intersection and turn there.
Change lanes safely and back up to the original intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane, drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: How can you avoid road rage?

options.text: Leave extra time for your trip.
Start your trip at the last moment.
Do not plan your trip ahead of time.
Assume nothing will slow you down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave extra time for your trip.
questions.explanation: Plan ahead and leave extra time. This way, if traffic slows you down, you will not feel rushed. Stay calm and drive friendly.

questions.question: What should you do when someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is available.
If no right lane is available, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear so the driver can pass you.
Never stop suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: If someone tailgates you, move right if you can. If not, slow down gradually when it is safe so they can pass. Never stop suddenly because this increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in an alley unless a different speed is posted?

options.text: 15 mph.
30 mph.
45 mph.
55 mph.

questions.explanation: The speed limit in an alley is 15 miles per hour. Follow any posted speed limit signs if they show a different speed.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Winding road ahead.
Pedestrian crossing.
Low ground railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: This sign means railroad tracks cross the road at a steep angle. Low vehicles may drag or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: What should you do if you are in a serious car crash?

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is hurt.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible. Call 911 if anyone is hurt. You must report the crash to police if someone is injured, someone dies, or there is more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle on the right shoulder?

options.text: Never.
When the car in front is driving too slowly.
When the car in front is turning.
When the shoulder is unpaved.

questions.explanation: Never pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder. You must stay on the main paved road when passing.

questions.question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving:

options.text: Do not make driving errors.
Have trouble driving slowly.
Are better drivers because they are not hungry.
Have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. This makes it harder to control your vehicle and stay in your lane.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers going too fast for road conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers keeping a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for the conditions. Always drive at or below the speed limit and slow down when conditions are bad.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.
Right turns are not allowed.
Left turns are allowed.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It tells you that right turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: This sign prevents:

options.text: Entering full parking lots.
Entering road construction areas.
Entering dead-end streets.
Entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is one-way. Do not enter from your current direction.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means:

options.text: The same as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to stop completely.
Road conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: Driving at night compared to driving during the day is:

options.text: Less dangerous.
Just as dangerous.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. You cannot see as well in the dark, headlights can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers may be on the road.

questions.question: When driving up a hill behind a heavy truck, you should know:

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to pass the truck safely.
You may not be able to pass the truck legally.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles often go slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. When visibility is limited on a hill, you cannot legally pass. You may also not be able to pass safely.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a sharp curve ahead in the direction of the arrow. Multiple signs may be placed throughout a long curve.

questions.question: Highway signs that warn about dangerous conditions are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.explanation: Warning signs tell drivers about possible dangers ahead. Always follow warning signs. Ignoring them can cause accidents.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a crosswalk.

options.text: 20 feet
30 feet
35 feet
45 feet

questions.explanation: Do not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk. A badly parked car can cause a crash.

questions.question: What do large flashing arrow panels mean?

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.
Look in the direction the arrow points.
You can stay in your current lane.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.
questions.explanation: Large flashing arrow panels are used in construction zones where a lane is closed. Slow down and merge in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: Work zone signs mean:

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop and back up right away.
Driving conditions are not safe.
Drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and show that work is happening on or near the road. Be very careful when you see these signs.

questions.question: You are coming to a railroad crossing with flashing signals. You should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing signals, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs like lowered gates or the sound of a train.

questions.question: When involved in a crash, you should:

options.text: Move injured people far from the road.
Do not move injured people unless absolutely necessary.
Tell injured people they are fine and do not need help.
Move injured people where they want to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move injured people unless absolutely necessary.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people. Only move them if there is fire or immediate danger. Keep them lying or sitting down until medical help arrives.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow line to pass another car?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the car ahead is going slower than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean do not pass. You can only cross them to turn into a driveway or business entrance. No passing is allowed over solid yellow lines.

questions.question: Before turning left, it is important to:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Let oncoming cars go first.
Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait for oncoming traffic to get a red light.

questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic light, let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go first.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another car is coming toward you. Your headlights should be:

options.text: On high beam.
On low beam.
Off. Use parking lights instead.
On either high or low beam.

questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when another car is coming toward you or in front of you. Use low beams to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. This includes changing lanes, pulling into a parking space, and pulling into traffic from a parked position.
